ai.summary: Reuters reported that roughly 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong while China withholds approval for large-scale imports. The situation highlights tensions between Chinese demand for AI computing and concerns about reliance on U.S. technology.
ai.title: Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval

ai.summary: OpenAI said an automated research pipeline using an upcoming cyber model identified 948 distinct Linux-kernel local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities and generated candidate patches. The company said the work involved validation in isolated virtual machines and that reports were being shared with maintainers.
ai.title: OpenAI says pipeline found and exploited 948 Linux flaws

ai.summary: AI-driven demand for semiconductor production is boosting business for chemical and industrial-gas suppliers, Reuters reported, citing recent company results and investment plans. The growth reflects the expanding manufacturing supply chain behind AI chips.
ai.title: AI chip demand powers third-quarter growth at chemical, industrial gas makers

ai.summary: Reuters reported that companies and executives say AI is accelerating cyber threats and making attacks more sophisticated, intensifying pressure to strengthen defenses. The report cites incidents and security concerns across multiple sectors.
ai.title: AI sharpens cat-and-mouse hacking battle as companies strengthen defences

ai.summary: A Reuters report on U.S. midterm ballot measures examined voters’ concerns about AI in classrooms and technology policy. It also noted Google’s decision to make Gemini off by default for school-student accounts, while allowing administrators to opt in.
ai.title: In midterm ballot measures, voters send a message to AI builders

ai.summary: A roundup reported that Google DeepMind unveiled Genie 4, a research system that generates interactive virtual worlds from text instructions in real time. The report describes the work as early-stage, with limitations in long predictions and gaps between generated environments and reality.
ai.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model

quantum.summary: IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge National Laboratory launched a platform combining IBM quantum processors with Oak Ridge high-performance computing to test quantum error-correction methods. The effort is intended to speed research toward the U.S. Department of Energy’s goal of a scientifically useful quantum computer by late 2028.
quantum.title: IBM, AMD, Oak Ridge launch quantum error-correction platform

quantum.summary: Quint Computing, a startup founded by FAU researchers, raised €9.1 million in seed funding to develop quantum processors with an architecture designed to reduce error-correction overhead. The university says the financing is the largest seed round to date for a German quantum-computing company.
quantum.title: Quantum computing: Over 9 million euros for FAU start-up

quantum.summary: A preprint by researchers including members of Alice & Bob estimates that a future system with 22,593 superconducting cat qubits could factor an RSA-2048 key in about 3.14 days under its assumptions. The result is a theoretical resource estimate, not a demonstration that such a machine exists or can currently break RSA encryption.
quantum.title: Factoring RSA Integers with the Cat Qubit Code

quantum.summary: IQM reported €42.2 million in new third-quarter orders and a €102.5 million backlog, up 52% from the start of 2026. Its largest deal was a €33 million contract for a system intended to support error-correction research and logical qubits at CSC’s LUMI AI Factory in Finland.
quantum.title: Interim Report for Q3 2026

quantum.summary: Quantinuum outlined a roadmap for its Nexus developer platform, aiming to add capabilities for building and running applications on increasingly error-corrected hardware. The company’s roadmap extends through Apollo, which it says it plans as a universal fault-tolerant quantum computer for 2029.
quantum.title: Quantinuum Unveils Nexus Roadmap to Deliver the First Developer Platform Designed for the Fault-Tolerant Quantum Era

quantum.summary: Horizon Quantum signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Singapore-based Entropica Labs for an anticipated $27 million in shares, subject to due diligence and definitive agreements. Entropica develops software for fault-tolerant quantum computing, including its Loom compiler.
quantum.title: Horizon Quantum Signs Non-Binding Letter of Intent to Acquire Entropica Labs
